Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, trunk: tigers and medallions read at full size
Whole body only with a solid number plate
Numbers need a solid black or white plate; straight on the brocade they are unreadable.
Almost nothing: this is finished artwork, leave it alone
Pairs well with: black, gold, deep blue, white.
pitfalls: Not a take-your-colour base: black, white and gold are baked in
Not plain silver or gold: it is a multicolour picture with a black ground
Avoid: white numbers vanish on pale ground, avoid next to other ornate brocades.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 190 (true metallic), roughness 49 (high gloss), clearcoat 31 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: white numbers vanish on pale ground, avoid next to other ornate brocades.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: this is finished artwork, leave it alone; at most a plain plate for numbers: any added motif drowns in the brocade
Patterns to avoid: any pattern or flake overlay: the surface is already fully dense
Spec overlays that work: none worth adding: the spec map follows the artwork
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
